{{short description|Indian mathematician (1946–2014)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=July 2019}}
'''Vikram Bhagvandas Mehta''' (August 15, 1946 – June 4, 2014) was an Indian mathematician who worked on algebraic geometry and vector bundles. Together with [[Annamalai Ramanathan]] he introduced the notion of [[Frobenius split]] varieties, which  led to the solution of several problems about [[Schubert varieties]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Bhagvandas Mehta|first=Vikram|last2=Ramanathan|first2=Annamalai|date=July 1985|title=Frobenius splitting and cohomology vanishing for Schubert varieties|url=https://annals.math.princeton.edu/?s=Vikram+Bhagvandas+Mehta&search-field=|journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]]|volume=122|issue=1|pages=27–40|doi=10.2307/1971368|issn=0003-486X|jstor=1971368|url-access=subscription}}</ref> He is also known to have worked, from the 2000s onward, on the [[fundamental group scheme]]. In 2002, he and Subramanian published a proof of a conjecture by [[Madhav V. Nori]]<ref name=":Nori">M. V. Nori ''On the Representations of the Fundamental Group'', Compositio Mathematica, Vol. 33, Fasc. 1, (1976), p. 29-42</ref> that brought back into the limelight the theory of this object that until then had met with little success.<ref name=":Vikram">V. B. Mehta, S. Subramanian ''On the Fundamental Group Scheme'', Inventiones mathematicae, 148, 143-150 (2002)</ref>

== Awards ==
The [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]] awarded him the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize for Science and Technology]] in 1991 for his work in algebraic geometry.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Awardee Details: Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize|url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/content/Detail.aspx?AID=187|access-date=2020-10-19|website=ssbprize.gov.in}}</ref>
